highlights: **Performance:** New worktrees refresh their Git index once instead of repeatedly re-hashing files. PR checks avoid full thread histories; terminal focus avoids whole-sidebar renders, and idle Find releases searched text.

**Server updates:** Committed updates repoint the service unit to the selected runtime. Database backups can copy while the server is running when cloning is unavailable; desktop shutdown waits for its local server.

**Agent reliability:** Provider-instance switches preserve active turns, stopping turns keep queued sends, and delegated task cancellation reports interruption. Imported ACP sessions retain native history; OpenCode tracks shell and image jobs.

**Mobile:** Code blocks regain syntax colours, question-card file links open the viewer, and subscription widgets stop expiring against already-reset windows. Images opened by agents remain visible across clients.

**Chat and navigation:** Screen-reader announcements expose agent messages and steps. Questions can be answered while normal sends are blocked; diff selections and Viewed files survive navigation, and PR links target the named location.

**Desktop and remote:** Clear stale GPU caches after Electron upgrades, retry reconnecting environments, and reuse known machine addresses for link requests. Open in runs locally when the desktop shares a background server's T3 home.

**Projects and search:** Quoted phrase search finds messages and comments. Cloned repository URLs use their own folders, scheduled-task edits retain workspaces, and worktree branch comparisons no longer inherit the base branch's PR.

**Reviews and usage:** Watched GitHub PRs react to host events. GitLab adds merged-request reverts and line-range review comments; Claude subagent output counts correctly, and Grok/Cursor usage gains pace indicators.
